To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we report the first case of a TSC-2 mutant GBM in an adolescent patient with Li-Fraumenis syndrome.

(1) we report the case of a TSC-2 mutated GBM that was successfully treated with everolimus, (2) we describe the use of whole exome and whole transcriptome sequencing in a child with a brain tumour, and (3) we describe the benefit of precision oncology for children with brain tumours.
we identified a novel targetable mutation in a child with GBM and achieved durable remission with precision medicine therapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effects of everolimus on the proliferation, invasion and migration of glioma cell lines.
the identification of new molecular targets in glioma and the development of novel therapies for glioma.
the study of the molecular mechanisms of the development of the human brain, and the study of the mechanisms of brain diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is a single case of a patient with GBM with a germline TP5 mutation, and a somatic TSC 2 mutation, who had a complete response to treatment with everolimus and is currently in remission.
this is the first report of a child with GBM who achieved a durable remission with a mTOR inhibitor.
the use of everolimus in the treatment of TSC2-mutation-positive GBM in a child is effective, but further studies are needed to confirm these findings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
precision medicine in paediatric GBM can be successful, but that it requires a team of experts and a multidisciplinary approach.
the use of a targeted agent for the treatment of a TSc2-mutant GBM in a patient with Li Fraumeni syndrome is feasible and may be beneficial.
the patient's tumour was treated with everolimus and he has had a complete remission for over 30 months.
The main takeaway from our work is that
precision medicine can be used in children to identify targetable mutations that may be amenable to targeted therapies.
precision medicine should be offered to all children diagnosed with GBM, as it may lead to a more effective treatment strategy.
precision medicine can be used to guide treatment decisions in children with high-risk brain tumours.
